paper_title: O1-Pruner Length-Harmonizing Fine-Tuning for O1-Like Reasoning Pruning
caption: Comparison of inference time-cost on MATH among different models and methods. achieves the shortest inference times (slightly over 1 minute for Marco-o1-7B and 4 minutes for QwQ-32B-Preview), demonstrating its effectiveness in accelerating long-thought model inference for both small and large long thought models.
model_annotation: The chart presents a side-by-side comparison of inference times in minutes for two models, Marco-o1-7B and QwQ-32B-Preview, under five different methods: Baseline (light green), Fast-Solving Prompt (yellow), SFT (gray), DPO (orange), and O1-Pruner (blue). For each model, the horizontal bars represent the inference time, with the vertical axis labeled “Inference Time (minute)” and a linear scale ranging from 0 to 7 minutes. The bars are arranged vertically with the shortest at the bottom and the longest at the top, sorted in descending order of inference time. For Marco-o1-7B, the O1-Pruner method (blue bar) shows the shortest inference time at approximately 1.1 minutes, followed by DPO (orange, ~1.5 minutes), SFT (gray, ~2.1 minutes), Fast-Solving Prompt (yellow, ~2.1 minutes), and Baseline (light green, ~2.2 minutes). For QwQ-32B-Preview, the O1-Pruner method (blue bar) has the shortest inference time at 4.0 minutes, followed by DPO (orange, ~5.7 minutes), SFT (gray, ~5.9 minutes), Fast-Solving Prompt (yellow, ~5.0 minutes), and Baseline (light green, ~6.0 minutes). The bars are grouped by model, with the legend indicating the color coding for each method.
